thread:
Maya (PM): Heads up — Big customer asked us to prioritize Optimize toolkit features. They pushed for quantization first to cut costs, but infra folks argue batching gives immediate latency/cost wins. Need a quick triage for next sprint and a decision on sequencing. Anyone free for a fast call?

Sam (Eng): Can we do a quick RICE scoring here? Impact vs effort is the right frame. My gut: batching is low-mid effort, immediate throughput gains. Quant is high impact but high effort + eval risk. Caching is low effort but benefit depends on workload.

Lee (ML): FWIW quantization can give 2-3x memory reduction on our Llama-family variants but can introduce subtle quality regressions. We'll need eval suites and rollback thresholds. Also some model ops require custom quant configs per architecture.

Anya (ProdOps): If we ship batching first we can wire autoscaling + burst capacity and customers see unit-cost improvements quickly. Launch criteria idea: p95 latency <= 1.2x baseline AND token unit cost improvement >= 10% in canary. Also need smoke test for KV-cache correctness.

Maya (PM): OK — let's put quick RICE numbers in-thread (1-5 scale). Drop one line each and we'll tally. I'll compile and make a spec doc after.

Sam (Eng): ```
Feature | Reach | Impact | Confidence | Effort(1-5)
Batching | 4 | 3 | 4 | 2
Caching | 3 | 2 | 3 | 1
Quantization | 2 | 5 | 3 | 5
```
(rough estimates; Effort 1=low ..5=high)

Lee (ML): Agree with numbers-ish. Add: Quant confidence lower for older models; need eval harness with prompt sets + sampling checks. Suggest parallelize quant R&D but not block customer-facing wins.

Anya (ProdOps): I'll add operational constraints: feature flags, canary dashboard, checklist: ingestion test, p50/p95 latency, token cost, regression alerting. Rollout plan: canary -> 50% -> 100% over 2 weeks if no quality regressions.

Sam (Eng): Proposed sequencing based on RICE and ops risk: 1) Batching (pilot, 1 sprint) 2) Caching (quick follow-up, patch) 3) Quantization (research + guarded rollout). This gets customers faster wins while we do safe quant experiments.

Maya (PM): Decision (tentative): Run batching pilot this sprint, add caching as next sprint quick win, and run quantization as a parallel research track with strict eval gates. Deliverables: spec + acceptance criteria, small canary, dashboards, canary rollout playbook.

Lee (ML): I'll own the quant eval checklist. Will add required prompt suites, baseline sampling metrics, and acceptable degradation thresholds (e.g., <1% top-level quality delta on key tasks).

Anya (ProdOps): I'll create canary dashboards and the rollout playbook. Need an issue for infra work on continuous batching + autoscaler presets.

Maya (PM): @Sam please draft acceptance criteria for batching (latency & cost targets + smoke tests). @Lee add eval checklist in the same doc. I'll combine and circulate by EOD.

release-bot: created issue OPT-324: "optimize-toolkit/batching-pilot" :white_check_mark:

Sam (Eng): Will do. Quick ask: do we want a small subset of customers (5) for the pilot or internal only? I vote 5 real customers to validate economics.

Maya (PM): 5 real customers works — ProdOps to coordinate opt-in. Thanks all, I'll write the spec and RICE table and link here when ready. :rocket:
